name: Mars transit

gravity.note: NASA: crews are weightless on the six-month trek between the planets. On Mars itself NASA gives three-eighths (hazards page) or about one-third (gravity page) of Earth's gravity; that applies to the Mars base profile, not transit.

radiation_rate.note: Galactic cosmic rays measured by Curiosity's RAD instrument inside the spacecraft on its 2011-2012 cruise to Mars. Uncrewed vehicle; no crewed measurement exists.

comm_delay.unit: min one way (57 min round trip)
comm_delay.note: Team choice, conservative. It exceeds NASA's stated maximum of up to 20 minutes one way.

evacuation.note: No NASA page read states this outright. NASA: crews must handle situations with minimal support from teams on Earth.

medical_kit.note: No published medical kit for a Mars vehicle. Orion (Artemis II, a Moon mission) carries a medical kit for minor needs; not used as a Mars value.

exercise_kit.value: not confirmed for a Mars vehicle
exercise_kit.note: Reference only: Orion for Artemis II has a flywheel device, with 30 minutes of exercise per astronaut per day.

crew_size.note: Artemis II flies four astronauts around the Moon. No crew size is set for a Mars mission.

duration.note: NASA: astronauts bound for Mars would be leaving our planet for roughly three years.

dust.note: Planetary dust is a surface hazard; no source read states the transit value.

closed_habitat.note: NASA HRP hazards: isolation and confinement, and hostile closed environments inside a spacecraft.

delay_label: team value: 28.5 min one way / 57 min round trip (above NASA's stated 20 min maximum)
spec4_note: Spec 4 fields. crew: Spec 1 replay crew ids, size per crew_size (team value). equipment: every item the CPR and chest-pain protocols use, assumed on board so no step is hidden; not confirmed for a Mars vehicle (team value). delay: comm_delay in seconds (team value, above NASA's stated 20 min maximum).
